results.name: Decline Push Up Against Wall
instructions: Begin by placing your feet against a wall and positioning your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart. Your body should be in a decline position with your feet elevated on the wall.
Engage your core and ensure your body forms a straight line from your head to your feet.
Lower your chest towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Push through your hands to return to the starting position, straightening your arms. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Ensure your hands are positioned directly under your shoulders when you lower yourself.
Perform the movement with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
Use a stable wall to ensure your feet remain securely in place throughout the exercise.
results.description: Decline Push Up Against Wall is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Decline Push Up
instructions: Begin by placing your feet on a bench and position your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and ensure your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Lower your chest towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Push through your hands to return to the starting position, straightening your arms. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain a straight body line and avoid sagging your hips.
Use a stable chair or bench to prevent any movement or slipping during the exercise.
Perform the movement with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
results.description: Decline Push Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Deep Push-Up
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands holding dumbbells on the floor, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Your feet should be on the floor, forming a straight line from your head to your heels.
Engage your core and ensure your body forms a straight line from your head to your heels.
Lower your chest towards the floor by bending your elbows, allowing your chest to go deeper than your hands.
Push through your hands to return to the starting position, straightening your arms. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain a straight body line and avoid sagging your hips.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you push up and inhaling as you lower down.
Perform the movement with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
results.description: Deep Push-Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Alternate Bench Press (High Start)
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor and a dumbbell in each hand. Start with both arms extended straight up over your chest, palms facing forward.
Lower the right dumbbell towards your chest by bending your elbow while keeping the left arm extended and stable.
Press the right dumbbell back to the starting position by extending your elbow and contracting your chest muscles.
Repeat the movement with the left arm while keeping the right arm extended and stable. Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Lower the dumbbell in a controlled manner to avoid using momentum.
Breathe out as you press the dumbbell up and breathe in as you lower it down.
Ensure your feet remain flat on the floor to maintain stability.
results.description: Dumbbell Alternate Bench Press (High Start) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Around Pullover
instructions: Lie on your back on a bench with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended straight on your sides, palms facing down.
Slowly raise the dumbbells in an arc over your torso and behind your head, keeping your arms straight.
Return your arms back to the starting position in an arc motion, this time from your sides.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, ensuring a smooth and controlled motion throughout the exercise.
tips: Focus on using your chest and shoulder muscles to control the movement, avoiding any swinging or using momentum.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms throughout the exercise.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to protect your joints.
results.description: Dumbbell Around Pullover is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Back.

results.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie flat on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended above your chest and palms facing forward.
Engage your core and keep your feet flat on the floor, maintaining a natural arch in your lower back.
Lower the dumbbells to your chest by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms at a 45-degree angle to your torso.
Push the dumbbells back to the starting position by straightening your arms, ensuring a controlled motion throughout. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your wrists straight and aligned with your forearms throughout the exercise.
Avoid flaring your elbows too much; maintain a 45-degree angle to protect your shoulder joints.
Breathe in as you lower the dumbbells and exhale as you press them back up.
results.description: Dumbbell Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Chest Press Decline
instructions: Lie on a decline bench with your feet securely placed under the footpads. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended above your chest, palms facing forward.
Lower the dumbbells slowly towards your chest by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms at a 45-degree angle to your body.
Push the dumbbells back to the starting position by straightening your arms, squeezing your chest at the top of the movement.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the exercise.
tips: Ensure your feet are securely positioned under the footpads to prevent slipping during the movement.
Maintain a steady and controlled motion, avoiding any jerking or sudden movements.
Breathe in as you lower the dumbbells and exhale as you press them back up.
results.description: Dumbbell Chest Press Decline is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Chest Pull Over
instructions: Lie crosswise on a bench, with your upper back and shoulders supported, feet firmly planted on the floor and hips slightly lowered. Hold a dumbbell with both hands above your chest, arms slightly bent.
Slowly lower the dumbbell in an arc over your head and down towards the floor, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Bring the dumbbell back up to the starting position by reversing the arc motion, focusing on engaging your chest and lats.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the exercise.
tips: Keep a firm grip on the dumbbell to maintain control and prevent it from slipping.
Avoid lowering the dumbbell too far to prevent shoulder strain.
Engage your core to stabilize your body and support your lower back.
results.description: Dumbbell Chest Pull Over is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Decline Alternate Bench Press
instructions: Begin by lying on a decline bench with your feet secured and a dumbbell in each hand, arms lowered and elbows bent at a 90-degree angle, palms facing forward.
Press the left dumbbell upward until your arm is fully extended while keeping the right arm lowered.
Lower the left dumbbell back to the starting position, and press the right dumbbell upward until your arm is fully extended.
Alternate the press with each arm, maintaining control and stability throughout the exercise, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid locking your elbows at the top of the movement to keep tension on your muscles.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
Focus on a slow and controlled motion to maximize muscle engagement.
results.description: Dumbbell Decline Alternate Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Decline Bench Press
instructions: Begin by lying on a decline bench with your feet secured and a dumbbell in each hand, arms lowered and elbows bent at a 90-degree angle, palms facing forward.
Press both dumbbells upward simultaneously until your arms are fully extended, keeping the motion controlled.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with controlled motion until your elbows are at a 90-degree angle.
Repeat the press and lowering motion for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining stability throughout the exercise.
tips: Keep your feet firmly planted and secured to avoid slipping.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows at the top of the movement to protect your joints.
Concentrate on using your chest muscles to press the weights, minimizing shoulder involvement.
results.description: Dumbbell Decline Bench Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.
